bio:
Henry J. Meier was born 15 Nov 1866 in Germany (Baden), the fourth child and second son of Friedrich Mayer, mason, and Maria Anna Birkenmaier of Munzingen near Freiburg. His German birth/baptism record has not been located (he was born after his parents' 1862 Munzingen marriage; the Munzingen 1866 birth register L 10 Nr. 1591 should hold it — not yet read). By his own account in the 1910 census he immigrated in 1868; the family crossed together (Friedrich, Maria and four small children) between Nov 1866 and Sept 1869; ship and port not found. He appears as 'Henry, 4, Baden' in the 1870 census (Hazleton East Ward, 8 Jun 1870, 'Meyer' household) and 'Henry, 14, son, at school, born Baden' in 1880 ('Myer' household, Hazleton East Ward). On 10 Feb 1892 a licence was issued (Luzerne Orphans' Court marriage docket No. 11054) for Henry J. Meier, born in Germany 15 Nov 1866, residing in Hazleton, moulder, not previously married, and Annie A. Higgins, born New Philadelphia, PA, 2 Oct 1867, residing in Hazleton; they married 1 Mar 1892 at Hazleton (officiant read as 'Rev. Nich. Fo[rve?]' in the Meier notes and 'Rev. Nich. Gow…' in the Irish/PA notes). This docket is the first record spelling the name 'Meier' — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it. Sons Fred (1892) and Henry Jr. (1894) were born in Hazleton; Mary (1897) and Madeline (1900) in Wilkes-Barre (Ward 16, 1897–1900, FS tree); the family was in Tamaqua, Schuylkill Co. c.1903–06 (William b. c.1904; Joseph John b. 30 Jun 1906), near Anna's birthplace. In 1910 (Wilkes-Barre Ward 14, ED 158, sheet 20B, 28 Apr 1910, 14 Mill Street, dwelling 376, family 388) he was Henry J. Meier, head, 43, married 19 years, born Germany, both parents born Germany, immigrated 1868, citizenship 'Pa' (first papers only), moulder in a moulding shop, renting; Annie 42 had borne 7 children, 6 living. In 1920 (Ward 15, ED 262, sheet 6A, 7–8 Jan 1920, 298 Barney St, renting) he was 53, molder at an iron works — but this sheet gives his birthplace as 'New York' (informant error; every other record says Germany/Baden); son Henry Jr. lived next door at 296 Barney. In 1926 he was 'Henry', moulder, of Wilkes-Barre (William's application, which wrongly says born 'Penna.'). In 1940 (Ward 15, ED 40-330, sheet 3B, 3 Apr 1940, 16 Barney Street, owned, worth $3,000; same house in 1935) he was 'Meyer, Henry J., 72, born Germany, naturalized ("Na"), moulder at an iron works', with Anna A. (72), Mary C. (42) and Joseph J. (33). The citizenship change from 'Pa' (1910) to 'Na' (1940) implies his own naturalization between 1910 and 1940 (papers not found). He died, per the FamilySearch tree LTHM-1XV citing the Find a Grave index (QVG4-98K8), in Dec 1940 in Wilkes-Barre and was buried at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Township. He is NOT in the PA death index for 1939, 1940 or 1941 under Soundex M600 (Meier/Meyer/Maier/Mayer/Moore) as Henry or Harry in Luzerne (the only 1940 'Henry J Meyer' is in Erie, county 25, d. 18 Nov 1940, p.1426), nor in the NYS (ex-NYC) index 1931–71 at a fitting age; no Henry/Harry Meier in the Wilkes-Barre newspaper death lists 1929–40 and 1945. Possible explanations: a late-filed or misspelled certificate (Heinrich, Mier), or the tree's '1940' merged with Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick), 47, d. 9 Feb 1940 Wilkes-Barre. Two Long Island Henry Meier deaths (Huntington 21 Jul 1931, cert. 44888; Hempstead 24 May 1937, cert. 34005) were flagged as leads before the 1940 census proved him alive on 3 Apr 1940 — they cannot be him. A FamilySearch 'Henry Higgins (1866–1940)' (MWTJ-M9C) with identical dates is an unrelated man born in Bethnal Green, London, buried in Outremont, Quebec.

Henry J. Meier did not die in 1940. The 1950 census, taken on 8 Apr 1950, lists him at house 16 [Barney Street], Wilkes-Barre, as 'Meier, Henry J.', head, 83, married, born Germany, naturalized. With him were his wife Anna, 82, and their unmarried daughter Mary, 51, a saleswoman in a retail clothing store ([R4-S1]). Age 83 fits his birth of 15 Nov 1866 exactly. The Pennsylvania death index for 1950 has 'HARRY J MEIER', Wilkes-Barre, county 40, died 20 Dec 1950, certificate file 104173 ([R4-S2]). 'Harry' was the usual nickname for Henry; his son Henry James Jr. appears as 'Harry J.' in the 1920 and 1940 censuses and in the 1957 death index. That son died in 1957, and the other local Harry J. Meier (b. c.1904 New York, of Bear Creek Twp.) was not of Wilkes-Barre. The FamilySearch tree's 'December 1940' (from the Find a Grave index) is almost certainly a one-digit error for December 1950. That explains why earlier rounds found nothing in the 1939–41 indexes. He died aged 84, ten months before his wife Anna (d. 6 Oct 1951), and is buried at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Township (FS tree / Find a Grave index, as before).

facts.label: Surname
facts.value: Surname spelling history (Mayer→Meier): Munzingen registers write Mayer 1820–1862 (1820 marriage 'Henericus Mayer', 1835 birth 'Friedrich Mayer', 1862 marriage 'Friedrich Mayer'); 1870 US census 'Meyer, Frederick'; 1880 census 'Myer, Friedrich'; the 1892 Luzerne marriage docket No. 11054 is the first record spelling it 'Meier' (Henry J. Meier) — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it; 'Meier' is consistent from 1910 on (1910, 1920, 1926, 1930, 1950 records; PA death indexes 1911/1913/1963) except 'Meyer, Henry J.' in the 1940 census; no formal name change is recorded.

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Name in the Ancestry tree: "Henry James MEIER MYER"; research uses "Henry J. Meier".

Resolved: Death conflict: tree '1940'; FS tree Dec 1940; not in PA death index 1939–41 → He was alive in the 1950 census (aged 83) and is very probably the 'Harry J Meier' who died in Wilkes-Barre on 20 Dec 1950 (PA death index, file 104173). '1940' is a typo for 1950.

Round 4 searched without result: WebSearch: Find a Grave Henry J. Meier 1866–1940 St. Mary's Hanover Twp (no match surfaced; findagrave blocked); FS GenealogyBank obituary image on son Harry's profile (HTTP 403)
Round 4: 1950 census shows Henry alive at 83 at 16 Barney St; PA death index 1950 has Harry J. Meier, Wilkes-Barre, d. 20 Dec 1950 (file 104173). The tree's Dec 1940 is a typo for Dec 1950.

funFacts: He was still listed with his family at 16 Barney Street at 83, after more than 50 years as an iron moulder.

His son Fred's 1917 draft card names Fred's employer as the Vulcan Iron Works, Wilkes-Barre, where Fred was a moulder. Henry's 1920 and 1940 census entries say only 'moulder, iron works', so it is a reasonable guess, not proven, that father and son worked at the same foundry.

conflicts.assessment: The 1950 census proves he was alive on 8 Apr 1950, so the 1940 date is wrong. The 20 Dec 1950 Wilkes-Barre index entry for 'Harry J Meier' matches the tree's month (December) and his town. Strong probable; the certificate (file 104173) would confirm age and parents.
